reader_notes: Read from the note text, bars 1-27, with dump.ts for the whole piece and a throwaway comparison script (voice against voice, shifted in time and pitch) to confirm the extent of the canons and of the transposed restatement; every call below was then checked by reading the passage. No published analysis was consulted. x = the right hand's first two bars, C B C D Eb G Ab Bb Ab F F Eb D C | B Ab G F Eb D C B C D C D D. C D (1:1.5-2:4.875). y = what the leader plays next, bars 3-4, against x in the bass: Eb D C D Eb F G G F . F | F Eb . D Eb Ab. F Bb F (3:1-4:4.75). The leader's bars 5-8 are further new lines, all copied by the follower; they are not named separately but given as bar numbers of the prime.

members.reason: The bass now leads with the whole of the prime's leading line a twelfth lower (11:1.5-20:4.75), and the right hand follows two bars later, an octave above the bass's line (13:1.5-20:4.75), copying it strictly: the canon is restated in the dominant with the voices exchanged (leader below, follower above; the two lines shifted -17 and +7 semitones, two octaves apart, so the counterpoint is at the octave). The leader's free bars 9-10 return as the bass's bars 19-20, exact. Changes: the bass's first two notes are Eb3 F3 (then G A Bb ...) instead of G F# (the head enters from the Eb harmony that ends the prime); and the right hand, silent in the prime's bars 1-2, has free counterpoint in bars 11-12 (D5 G5 D5 Eb5 C5 D5 Bb4 C5 ..., leading to the D7 of g).

members.reason: The right hand restates the leader's line from the beginning in the tonic, note for note (23:1.5-26:1.25 = 1:1.5-4:1.25). Where the prime had the bass silent, the bass now plays y (23:1 C3 e. D3 Eb3 F3 G3 G3 F3 . F3 | F3 Eb3. ..., head varied: C e. for Eb D C), so bars 23-24 are the prime's bars 3-4 with the voices exchanged; then the bass enters with x at 25:1.5 an octave below (= 3:1.5, an octave lower), exactly as in the prime, against y in the right hand. Both lines leave the prime at 26:1.5-26:3 for the final cadence.

cadences.reason: ii (8:3, Ab C F in both voices) - V6/5 (8:4: bass D4, right hand F5 Bb5 Ab5 Bb5) - I (9:1: Eb4 below G5). Inside the canon (the leader goes free here, the follower runs on to 10:4.75): a weak, inverted-dominant arrival, not a section close. In the exchanged restatement the corresponding moment (19:1) is an inverted tonic (Bb/D) and so not a cadence.

G7 (22:1 bass B3 under F5) ... bass G3 G2 (22:4) to C3 (23:1), right hand G5 to Eb5: root-position V-I with the third on top. It ends the link and the right hand starts the tonic return of x at once (23:1.5).

notes: Bars 1-20 are two statements of one ten-bar canon (c-Eb, then g-Bb with the voices exchanged), i.e. 20 of 27 bars are strict canon at the octave; the remaining bars are a two-bar link and a shortened tonic return. Because the second canon is the first transposed and exchanged, the piece is also invertible throughout bars 1-20, but this follows from the canon rather than from a separate countersubject, so 'double' is not given as a second kind. The texture leaves almost no room for cadences: the only root-position V-I arrivals in the tonic are at 23:1 and 27:1.
